<title>Mudavym Wave Four</title>
<meta name="description" content="Seven rebuilt pages behind their own flags, each with its screenshot, the verdict it answers, the roads not taken, and a place to record your call.">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:ital,opsz,wght@0,9..144,400;0,9..144,600;1,9..144,400&family=DM+Sans:wght@400;500;600&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;600&display=swap">
<style>
:root {
  --paper-0:#FAF7F1; --paper-1:#F3EFE6; --paper-2:#EAE4D8; --ink-1:#211C16; --ink-2:#4F473C; --ink-3:#7C7365;
  --seal:#1A5E6B; --seal-deep:#14515C; --seal-tint:rgba(26,94,107,.10); --seal-ring:rgba(26,94,107,.32);
  --calm:#6D28D9; --shot-frame:#D9D2C4;
  --serif:"Fraunces",Georgia,"Times New Roman",serif; --sans:"DM Sans","Plus Jakarta Sans",system-ui,sans-serif; --mono:"JetBrains Mono",ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,monospace;
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) {
  --paper-0:#15130F; --paper-1:#1D1813; --paper-2:#262019; --ink-1:#EFE7D9; --ink-2:#C0B6A5; --ink-3:#8E8576;
  --seal:#5FB0BC; --seal-deep:#7DC3CD; --seal-tint:rgba(95,176,188,.14); --seal-ring:rgba(95,176,188,.38); --calm:#A05CFF; --shot-frame:#3A3128;
} }
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --paper-0:#15130F; --paper-1:#1D1813; --paper-2:#262019; --ink-1:#EFE7D9; --ink-2:#C0B6A5; --ink-3:#8E8576;
  --seal:#5FB0BC; --seal-deep:#7DC3CD; --seal-tint:rgba(95,176,188,.14); --seal-ring:rgba(95,176,188,.38); --calm:#A05CFF; --shot-frame:#3A3128;
}
* { box-sizing:border-box }
body { margin:0; background:var(--paper-0); color:var(--ink-1); font-family:var(--sans); font-size:15px; line-height:1.5; }
a { color:var(--ink-1); text-decoration:underline; text-decoration-color:var(--seal); text-underline-offset:3px }
.wrap { max-width:1480px; margin:0 auto; padding:40px 32px 96px }
.masthead { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr auto; gap:24px; align-items:end; padding-bottom:18px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink-1); position:relative }
.masthead::after { content:""; position:absolute; left:0; right:0; bottom:-4px; height:1px; background:var(--ink-1) }
.wordmark { font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:600; font-size:20px; letter-spacing:-.01em }
.wordmark b { color:var(--seal) }
.masthead h1 { font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:400; font-size:44px; line-height:1.05; margin:10px 0 6px; letter-spacing:-.02em; text-wrap:balance }
.masthead .brief { max-width:68ch; color:var(--ink-2); margin:0 }
.state { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-3); text-align:right; line-height:1.7 }
.state b { color:var(--ink-1); font-weight:600 }
.toc { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px 18px; padding:18px 0 8px; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12px }
.toc a { text-decoration:none; color:var(--ink-2); border-bottom:1px solid var(--paper-2); padding-bottom:2px }
.toc a:hover, .toc a:focus-visible { color:var(--seal); border-color:var(--seal) }
.entry { padding:40px 0 8px }
.entry-head { display:grid; grid-template-columns:auto 1fr auto; gap:18px; align-items:baseline; margin-bottom:18px }
.route { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:13px; color:var(--seal); font-weight:600; letter-spacing:.02em }
.entry h2 { font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:400; font-size:34px; margin:0; letter-spacing:-.02em; line-height:1.1 }
.chips { display:flex; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap }
.chip { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; padding:4px 9px; border:1px solid var(--paper-2); border-radius:999px; color:var(--ink-2); background:var(--paper-1) }
.chip.pass { border-color:var(--seal-ring); color:var(--seal-deep) }
.chip.fail { border-color:#A03A2A; color:#A03A2A }
.chip.flag { color:var(--ink-3) }
.entry-body { display:grid; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.55fr) minmax(300px,.85fr); gap:28px; align-items:start }
.shot { margin:0; border:1px solid var(--shot-frame); background:var(--paper-1); border-radius:4px; overflow:hidden }
.shot img { display:block; width:100%; height:auto }
.shot figcaption { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:8px 10px; border-top:1px solid var(--shot-frame); font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-3) }
.shot .cap { margin-left:auto }
.noshot { padding:120px 24px; text-align:center; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-3) }
.ground-toggle { font:600 11px var(--mono); letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; padding:4px 10px; border:1px solid var(--paper-2); background:transparent; color:var(--ink-2); border-radius:999px; cursor:pointer }
.ground-toggle[aria-pressed="true"] { background:var(--seal); color:var(--paper-0); border-color:var(--seal) }
.rail { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:18px }
.block .label, .decide .label { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10.5px; letter-spacing:.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); margin-bottom:6px }
.block p { margin:0 0 8px; color:var(--ink-2); max-width:62ch }
.block ul { margin:0; padding-left:18px; color:var(--ink-2) }
.block li { margin:0 0 5px }
.verdict blockquote { margin:0; font-family:var(--serif); font-style:italic; font-size:19px; line-height:1.35; color:var(--ink-1); text-wrap:balance }
.verdict-kind { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; color:var(--seal); margin-top:6px; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase }
.lens { padding:12px 14px; background:var(--paper-1); border-left:3px solid var(--calm); border-radius:0 4px 4px 0 }
.proof li { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12px }
.decide { margin-top:6px; padding:14px; border:1px solid var(--paper-2); border-radius:6px; background:var(--paper-1) }
.choices { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr); gap:6px; margin-bottom:10px }
.choices button { font:600 12px var(--mono); letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; padding:9px 0; border:1px solid var(--paper-2); background:var(--paper-0); color:var(--ink-2); border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer }
.choices button[aria-pressed="true"] { background:var(--seal); color:var(--paper-0); border-color:var(--seal) }
.decide textarea { width:100%; font:14px var(--sans); padding:8px 10px; border:1px solid var(--paper-2); background:var(--paper-0); color:var(--ink-1); border-radius:4px; resize:vertical }
.decide-foot { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; margin-top:8px }
.decide .save { font:600 12px var(--mono); letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; padding:8px 16px; border:1px solid var(--ink-1); background:var(--ink-1); color:var(--paper-0); border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer }
.decide .save:disabled { opacity:.45; cursor:default }
.decide .status { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-3) }
button:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible, a:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--seal); outline-offset:2px }
.sketches { margin-top:28px }
.sketches .label { font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10.5px; letter-spacing:.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); margin-bottom:10px }
.sketch-row { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit, minmax(420px, 1fr)); gap:18px }
.sketch { margin:0; border:1px dashed var(--shot-frame); border-radius:4px; overflow:hidden; background:var(--paper-1) }
.sketch.live { border-style:solid }
.sketch img { display:block; width:100%; height:auto }
.sketch figcaption { padding:8px 10px; font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-2); border-top:1px dashed var(--shot-frame) }
.sketch figcaption b { font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:600; font-size:15px; color:var(--ink-1); margin-right:6px }
.rule-off { height:5px; border-top:1px solid var(--ink-1); border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink-1); margin-top:34px; opacity:.85 }
.foot { padding-top:28px; color:var(--ink-2); max-width:70ch }
.foot h3 { font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:400; font-size:24px; margin:0 0 8px }
@media (max-width: 1000px) { .entry-body { grid-template-columns:1fr } .masthead { grid-template-columns:1fr } .state { text-align:left } .entry-head { grid-template-columns:1fr } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .choices button, .ground-toggle { transition:background .16s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), color .16s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1) } }
</style>
<div class="wrap">
  <header class="masthead">
    <div>
      <div class="wordmark">Mudavym<b>.</b></div>
      <h1>Seven pages, built against your verdicts. Your call on each.</h1>
      <p class="brief">Every page below runs on real data from the Meyhouse Palo Alto tenant through a local gateway, captured at 1440 wide. Each is gated by its own mudavym_design_&lt;page&gt; flag, OFF for every restaurant in production. Nothing here is live until you say so.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="state">branch <b>feat/mudavym-design-p4</b> · main merged in · pushed · every builder and auditor done<br>pages <b>7</b> · second passes <b>7/7</b> · sketches <b>8</b> · large builds <b>4/4</b> audited (ADRs 0107–0110)<br>flags in production <b>none on</b> · reminders and Stripe <b>off by switch</b> · merge waits on you</div>
  </header>
  <nav class="toc"><a href="#reports">/reports</a><a href="#notifications">/notifications</a><a href="#recommendations">/recommendations</a><a href="#calendar">/calendar</a><a href="#settings">/settings</a><a href="#profile">/profile</a><a href="#cellar">/cellar · /wines · /beer · /whiskey · /cocktails</a></nav>
  
<section class="entry" id="reports">
  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/reports</div>
    <h2>Reports — a sheet of cuttings</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">MERGE · second pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_reports · off</span><span class="chip pass">31 web · 330 analytics tests</span><span class="chip pass">Sonnet re-audit: pass with nits</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="reports"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Reports — a sheet of cuttings — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Reports — a sheet of cuttings — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>Used to like today&#x27;s drag-to-rearrange canvas — where we can just swipe and change everything to its place. The new version is more modern. Some blocks moved, some actions removed, more graphs, more focus on the insights plus the reports part. Be more creative here.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Merge · 2026-08-29</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>[&quot;Second pass, to your asks (different graph types for different people; while arranging, change the graph type or the analysis itself; lots of deep detailed graphs; keep drag and drop; fix every honest-about gap for real). A cutting is now a question, not a chart: every analysis reduces to one view shape drawn by one renderer, which is what makes “Show instead” (eleven catalogued analyses, every one a real endpoint) and “Draw as” (line · bars · area · heatmap · scatter · table · figure, offered only where true of the data) possible — and keeps the honesty rules in one place, where a sentence outranks every graph type. Each cutting prints the window it speaks about under its title, with hover detail and the engine&#x27;s own thresholds drawn as reference lines. Drag AND resize stay, tested; your arrangement and each cutting&#x27;s drawing persist in your own preferences.\n\nThe gateway now withholds instead of inventing: cost of goods returns null with a sentence when no delivered order came back ($0 would claim the first); the forecast admits when no model fitted (the daily series was zero-filled, so a fourteen-day projection of nothing had been published as a prediction); a week of seven zero means returns a tie with no “busiest day” (the payload that used to answer Sunday as both busiest and quietest).&quot;]</p></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>Named house presets (a chef&#x27;s sheet, an owner&#x27;s sheet) — held so the two per-cutting switches could land uncluttered; filed as the next step.</li><li>A weekday × hour heat map — not built because no endpoint has hour grain; the exact endpoint shape is filed.</li><li>Basket and vendor-scorecard cuttings — real endpoints, held back because their payloads were not read closely enough to write a decoder that could not silently guess a field.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>Cost of goods, forecast and seasonality now return null or a tie with a sentence instead of a zero — fourteen new gateway tests each fail on the pre-fix tree.</li><li>Keyboard drag and resize are not supported by the grid library; everything else is keyboard-reachable.</li><li>The report generator stays disabled with its reason: the endpoint files a pending row nothing fills.</li><li>One select needs a local override to beat a global white-background rule in the app&#x27;s own stylesheet; filed.</li><li>About 3,600 lines across seventeen files, none over 700 — over the guidance, stated.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>The drag canvas has stopped being an advantage: Restaurant365 ships drag-and-drop plus prompt-to-chart and role-based dashboards, Lightspeed ships a drag-and-drop report builder, Tenzo ships per-role dashboards with threshold alerts, and MarginEdge wins by refusing the canvas entirely — one daily P&amp;L, emailed. So the differentiator cannot be *that blocks move*. It has to be what a block can prove. TradeZella&#x27;s P&amp;L calendar is the shape to steal — a month of days, each carrying its own real number — and Mudavym is the only product that can put a service in that cell and then open it into the receipts, counts, vendor messages and agent decisions underneath. Ship an opinionated house layout; let dragging be dissent, not assembly.</p></div>
      <div class="block proof"><div class="label">Proof</div><ul><li>vitest 31/31 (type switching, analysis switching, sheet codec v1 upgrade, three gateway shapes)</li><li>analytics 330/330 across 25 suites · absent-not-zero 14/14</li><li>curl-verified live: cogs null + basis, forecast modelFitted:false, seasonality tie:true</li><li>tsc clean web + gateway · guard PASS · emoji grep empty</li><li>Sonnet re-audit: pass with nits</li></ul></div>
      <div class="decide" data-slug="reports">
        <div class="label">Your call</div>
        <div class="choices">
          <button type="button" data-verdict="keep">Keep</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="rework">Rework</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="merge">Merge</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="hold">Hold</button>
        </div>
        <textarea rows="3" placeholder="What to change, what to keep, what you want to see next…"></textarea>
        <div class="decide-foot"><button type="button" class="save">Record</button><span class="status" role="status"></span></div>
      </div>
    </aside>
  </div>
  
  
  <div class="rule-off" aria-hidden="true"></div>
</section>
<section class="entry" id="notifications">
  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/notifications</div>
    <h2>Notifications — the day-book</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">REWORK · second pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_notifications · off</span><span class="chip pass">30 web · 237 gateway tests</span><span class="chip pass">Sonnet re-audit: every claim verified</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="notifications"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Notifications — the day-book — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Notifications — the day-book — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>/notifications needs re-transformations. Neither drawn direction is the answer… what survives as inspiration only: Federation&#x27;s density — it shows more of what is actually happening — and Editorial&#x27;s way of subduing the already-handled items so the page quiets down as it is worked.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Rework · 2026-08-29</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>Second pass, to your asks. The emojis you saw were never in the page — they were written by the producers into the stored titles (100 of 100 rows on production&#x27;s first page carry one). Twelve producer sites across the gateway and the orchestrator stopped writing them, a guard spec now fails on any new one, and the page strips a stored leading emoji and draws the register&#x27;s lucide mark in ink on both the line and the rail tally so the two can never disagree.</p><p>One-tap actions left the day-book for the dashboard rail, directly under Waiting on you (your call): the book is now only a book — it dropped a whole register read and its wax — and the standing actions sit where the day starts, tenant-keyed, with the same honest line that the workflow behind them is a stub.</p><p>The day-book itself is unchanged: one book, three registers, one direction of travel, with the two audit defects (tenant-scoped rule-off, hasMore from the deepest page) fixed and pinned by hook-level tests.</p></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>A · The three-column desk — Federation taken literally: the three registers side by side under a fixed count strip. Not built: a line would teleport between columns instead of moving down, and three live columns read as a monitoring wall — the security camera the müdavim story was written against.</li><li>B · The day-strip — a vertical time axis with the day&#x27;s lines hung off it and a scrubber like the dashboard&#x27;s tape. Not built: notification times cluster on the hour, so the axis is long stretches of nothing punctuated by knots, and it spends the whole page on the one dimension every row already states in five characters.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>Twelve notification producers no longer write emojis; three remain inside server log lines only, out of scope and recorded.</li><li>The command-palette entrance is not built: the palette&#x27;s registry is a shared component; filed.</li><li>A line stating its own rule and 90-day fire count, and quieting a line by settlement (the credit landed, the PO went out), have no gateway read behind them yet — drawn as proposed in the sketches, filed as the next two builds.</li><li>“Rule off every open line” names the active restaurant, so it can never rule off another tenant&#x27;s book.</li><li>“Set aside” is per-browser and says so.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>Linear is the state of the art and we are behind it: snooze (with auto-wake on new activity), hide-read, quick-search and a *separate* Triage queue with exactly four resolutions. Slack&#x27;s rebuild adds the density rule — batch only what the user isn&#x27;t looking at, per context, and reset on open. Restaurant tools stop at threshold email (Tenzo) or par-breach with an auto-order attached (MarketMan); MOXē alone notifies about the physical world, pinging when the truck is thirty minutes out. None of them can do the thing we can: subdue an item because *the world settled it* — the credit arrived, the PO went out — rather than because someone read it. Split &quot;needs a decision&quot; from &quot;what happened&quot;, and quiet the page by settlement.</p></div>
      <div class="block proof"><div class="label">Proof</div><ul><li>vitest 30/30 (notifications + dashboard panel)</li><li>jest 237/237 across notifications, team, communications</li><li>pytest 19/19 (orchestrator producer)</li><li>guard spec: 28 offences on the pre-fix tree, 0 now</li><li>tsc clean in owned dirs · guard PASS · emoji grep empty</li><li>Sonnet re-audit: every claim verified · coverage gaps closed (44 tests)</li></ul></div>
      <div class="decide" data-slug="notifications">
        <div class="label">Your call</div>
        <div class="choices">
          <button type="button" data-verdict="keep">Keep</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="rework">Rework</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="merge">Merge</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="hold">Hold</button>
        </div>
        <textarea rows="3" placeholder="What to change, what to keep, what you want to see next…"></textarea>
        <div class="decide-foot"><button type="button" class="save">Record</button><span class="status" role="status"></span></div>
      </div>
    </aside>
  </div>
  
  <div class="sketches"><div class="label">Sketches — example data, not a tenant. Screenshots only; nothing here is built.</div><div class="sketch-row"><figure class="sketch"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="The three-column desk — sketch with example data"><figcaption><b>The three-column desk</b> Federation taken literally: needs a hand · the house acted · ruled off side by side under a fixed count strip, every register the gateway produces populated, digests stacking, folded duplicates, the rail tallies and filters. <section class="entry" id="recommendations">
  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/recommendations</div>
    <h2>Recommendations — ruled by consequence</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">REWORK · second pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_recommendations · off</span><span class="chip pass">37 web · 330 analytics tests</span><span class="chip pass">Sonnet re-audit: blocker closed — cached insights now carry their generator version</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="recommendations"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Recommendations — ruled by consequence — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Recommendations — ruled by consequence — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>Likes the new version but wants more structure and more uniqueness. Maybe we should find another way.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Rework · 2026-08-29</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>[&#x27;Second pass, to your ask (“endpoints profoundly solid — Wednesday sales came in 100% lower than your average Wednesday; if dismissed, avoided at all costs, and tell them; or discard it from the analysis”). Your example sentence was a live bug: the running gateway really produced “Wednesday sales came in 100% lower than your average Wednesday ($0 vs $104)”, because the daily series filled a day with no rows with a literal zero — a closure and a dead day were the same number. Days with no rows are now unobserved: the weekday baseline skips to the latest observed day and dates the sentence, drops unobserved days from the history and re-applies the floor; week-over-week withholds unless both windows have enough observed days; a trend needs fourteen real days. Live re-read: zero sentences claiming a 100% drop.\n\nDismiss became a standing instruction the engine honours on every run (it had never read dismissals before). The sheet asks the scope — this exact finding (default) · this rule for this subject · this rule entirely — offers only the scopes the entry can support, carries the separate “also exclude this day from the analysis”, states the promise in words, and is undoable from History. The opening line now carries a second sentence: how many entries a dismissal withheld, or that the dismissal store could not be read. Standing reads the real first-fired date.&#x27;]</p></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>a · The run-sheet — one sheet banded by time-to-act (Tonight / This week / This month) with the register demoted to a filter, printed and carried to the pass. Probably the better page on a Friday — but it re-centres the page on urgency, the axis the legacy already had, so it answers “more structure” and not “more uniqueness”.</li><li>b · The two-pane docket — a narrow list of entries left, the full working pinned right. Reads beautifully with a long book and is dead space with a short one, and short is what a restaurant without POS coverage actually gets. Both are one refactor away; the register and the three-fact line survive either.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>The day-exclusions table exists only when its migration merges, so the “also exclude this day” checkbox renders disabled with that exact reason today, never hidden.</li><li>The subject and period scopes are unit-proven; only the rule scope could be proven end-to-end on the local tenant, whose firing entries name no subject.</li><li>A Settings panel listing rule-wide silences is filed, not built — the settings page belongs to another builder this pass.</li><li>“Let Mudavym do it” stays disabled on every entry: no autonomous path exists in the gateway.</li><li>Six of the new tests fail against the pre-fix engine — the zero-fill was real, not theoretical.</li><li>INSIGHT_GENERATOR_VERSION is bumped by hand and nothing enforces it yet — the checksum guard is filed, not built.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>Google Ads runs the most complete version of this page and shows exactly what to avoid: an optimization score that reaches 100% when you *dismiss* every recommendation — a queue-clearing metric wearing the clothes of business health, and practitioners&#x27; standard advice is to disable auto-apply. AWS Trusted Advisor is more honest: suppression is scoped, and inherited checks say they are not yours to silence. Toast IQ and Nory go the other way, executing changes straight from a feed. Mudavym&#x27;s advantage is the sentence already in its own source: deterministic rules, no LLM, auditable. Push it further — make the unit a case that closes with a measured outcome, and let a refusal retune the rule that produced it.</p></div>
      <div class="block proof"><div class="label">Proof</div><ul><li>vitest 37/37</li><li>67 new gateway tests · analytics module 330/330</li><li>gateway boots (check_gateway_boots.sh)</li><li>tsc clean in owned modules · guard PASS · emoji grep empty</li><li>live round trip: 3 shown → dismiss → 2 shown, suppressed 1 → restore → 3</li><li>Sonnet re-audit: blocker closed — the persisted insight cache was a third reader still serving the 100% sentence; every row now carries generator_version and a reader refuses anything older (76 gateway tests, 0 rows claiming 100% across all tenants)</li></ul></div>
      <div class="decide" data-slug="recommendations">

<section class="entry" id="calendar">
  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/calendar</div>
    <h2>Calendar — the day is the unit of record</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">KEEP · third pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_calendar · off</span><span class="chip pass">37 web · 90 calendar gateway tests</span><span class="chip pass">Build B audited: pass</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="calendar"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Calendar — the day is the unit of record — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Calendar — the day is the unit of record — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto · Feb 2026 data in the tenant</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>I really prefer the new version. That&#x27;s for sure.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Keep · the one page liked unreservedly · 2026-08-29</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>A KEEP is the hardest brief: there is nothing to fix, so the only honest way to spend the work is to make the page mean what the house means. One idea does that — the day is the unit of record, and deliveries are the spine. Month, Week, Day and Agenda are four magnifications of one book. Every view sorts deliveries first and gives them the seal rule; everything else gets an ink rule. A delivery that arrived is ruled off with the double rule, and a day whose whole delivery account is settled is ruled off as a day, under a dry-pressed seal. That single device replaces what a calendar normally does with colour, which is how the page keeps the one-chromatic-colour rule without going flat.</p><p>The header states the exact window being read and one italic sentence that says only what it knows (“5 other entries.” / “Nothing is written against this period.” / “— The book has not been read.”).</p><p>Third pass (large build B, ADR 0109): a reminder is the house&#x27;s job, not the browser&#x27;s. Idempotency is a database index, not a boolean — a claim row per entry and person is written before any send, so a reminder cannot go twice and quiet hours become a per-person deferral. The per-tenant job runs under the existing scheduler, writes a durable notification, and finally gives reminder_sent an honest writer. The reminder register now names the job&#x27;s last run, its next run and whether the scheduler serves this house at all. The job ships OFF behind an environment allow-list, deliberately not the design flag, because it writes to every member&#x27;s inbox and phone; live status against production reads served, not armed, nothing pending, so arming it sends nothing retroactively.</p></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>1 · The delivery board — demote the grid to a locator and make the primary object a board of deliveries by state (expected → in transit → arrived → ruled off). Follows the spine argument further. Not built because a board is not a calendar: you cannot answer “what is Thursday like” on it, and the four views are the thing you said to keep.</li><li>2 · The single-column day book — drop the month grid, one scrolling ledger of days with a month mini-map in the rail. The purest expression of the idea and the most Editorial. Not built because planning a week of deliveries needs the 14th and the 21st side by side.</li><li>The fork inside the build: the eight event-type colours are NOT a page colour system here — type colour survives only as a 7px swatch inside the type picker, and the grid draws rank instead. Honouring per-type colour on the grid is a real alternative that reads faster for a tenant with many custom types; judge it against the screenshot.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>The page does not reuse the shared calendar hooks: they return an empty list on failure, silently substitute an offline copy, and turn a real 4xx on write into a fabricated “saved offline” success — all three make absence look like health. This page reads through the authenticated client directly and says what failed.</li><li>The meeting-memo prompt is gone: it collected notes nothing stores.</li><li>A stored value outside the gateway&#x27;s own enum (production carries event_type &#x27;audit&#x27; and status &#x27;active&#x27;) is not coerced — the sheet says it is holding a value it cannot re-send, instead of rewriting your record under a green save.</li><li>Paging is reported: the first 100 of a busy month is never drawn as the whole month. Any ?limit= on the events endpoint returns 400 today (a DTO defect, filed), so every caller is stuck on the 100-row default.</li><li>The dispatch migration was written to the proven lock-down shape but could not be executed here (no local database); the audit says so rather than claiming it ran.</li><li>An entry created on the legacy page and never opened in the rebuilt sheet can still fire once from the browser poller the app boots at start-up — outside this build&#x27;s paths, filed.</li><li>Sub-day offsets (the column holds whole days) and email reminders (no safe recipient policy yet) are not built; both are said on the row.</li><li>Arming the job is your call: CALENDAR_REMINDERS_ENABLED, filed as roadmap item 19.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>Restaurant calendars in this field are scheduling calendars: 7shifts hangs events off the roster with a permission and a dated Manager Log Book; Fourth generates the week from a POS-plus-weather forecast; Lightspeed adds a shift logbook. None of them draw the clock that actually governs a kitchen&#x27;s buying — every vendor&#x27;s order cutoff and delivery days, which ordering software knows but files as *settings*. Notion Calendar shows what keyboard-first restraint looks like. Our page is already the strongest here (Month/Week/Day/Agenda, RRULE, reminders, vendor links), so the move is additive: put the cutoff windows on the grid as closing time, mark past days with what the ledger recorded, and label an inferred window as inferred.</p></div>
      <div class="block proof"><div class="label">Proof</div><ul><li>tsc --noEmit clean</li><li>seeded-defaults guard 0 violations on the dir</li><li>1,879 code lines + 635 CSS · seven files</li><li>nine gateway defects filed in §9, two red</li><li>Sonnet audit interrupted (session rate limit) — re-run pending</li><li>vitest 37/37 (27 next + legacy reminders test) · jest 90 calendar, 319 with notifications + communications</li><li>curl: reminders/status 401 without bearer, 200 with; events?limit=500 200</li><li>gateway boots · guard 0 violations · emoji grep empty</li><li>Build B audited: pass — claim-before-send proven against a reverted copy; nits closed</li></ul></div>
      <div class="decide" data-slug="calendar">
        <div class="label">Your call</div>
        <div class="choices">
          <button type="button" data-verdict="keep">Keep</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="rework">Rework</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="merge">Merge</button>
          <button type="button" data-verdict="hold">Hold</button>
        </div>
        <textarea rows="3" placeholder="What to change, what to keep, what you want to see next…"></textarea>
        <div class="decide-foot"><button type="button" class="save">Record</button><span class="status" role="status"></span></div>
      </div>
    </aside>
  </div>

</section>
<section class="entry" id="settings">
  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/settings</div>
    <h2>Settings — ten registers</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">KEEP · Editorial · second pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_settings · off</span><span class="chip pass">22 web · 23 gateway tests</span><span class="chip pass">Sonnet re-audit: pass · all five blockers closed</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="settings"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Settings — ten registers — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Settings — ten registers — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>I kind of like the Editorial. I think that&#x27;s the best way to go — or Federation, it doesn&#x27;t matter. But I feel like there should be more.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Keep, Editorial · 2026-08-29</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>Second pass. The first audit failed this page on five provenance claims that were false, so the mechanism was rebuilt on measurement: every key rendered as “read by nothing” was grepped across all four runtimes (gateway, web, mobile, orchestrator). Quiet hours IS read by the notification agent — its control is back with the citing file beside it; push, the five categories and the four consents are written and read by nothing, and stay dead with the grep result as their reason. The four false “no last-changed date” lines are fixed at the source: chains and branches now return their real updated_at on every read path (and a rename stamps it, because the table has no update trigger), invites and the sign-off read their real dates, and the provenance line gained a verb — granted · issued · connected · last check — so a date is never mislabelled “changed”.</p><p>Eleven registers now (Cellar joined: the house&#x27;s declared registers, read from the cellar&#x27;s own control), each split into its own file; the note carries “what this page can do now, and what more means here” — every register&#x27;s effect, storage, permission and date in one table, plus the exact recipe for the settings audit trail nothing records today.</p></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>1 · Keep the legacy single-page scroll with the sticky tab bar — all ten registers stacked, scrollspy highlighting. Not built: the scrollspy rewrites ?tab= as you scroll, so the deep link you just followed is destroyed within a second, and ten registers carrying provenance run to four screens of dense text. If you want everything visible at once, this comes back with ?tab= read on arrival only.</li><li>2 · Leave the dead consents and category switches settable under a “recorded, not enforced” label. Not built: a switch whose only effect is to record itself is the fake toggle the brief rules out. But this is a capability removal on web, so it is genuinely your call — wire them as real gates, delete them, or restore the controls with the label.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>Nothing records who changed a setting; the page says so on its first screen, and the note gives the table and endpoint that would.</li><li>Push, five notification categories and four consents are stored and read by nothing; each is shown dead with the grep that proves it.</li><li>A new suspected production defect, filed not fixed: the team roster read orders by a column its table does not have and swallows the error into an empty list — the Team register says both possibilities instead of “nobody works here”.</li><li>The seven borrowed dialogs remain the shipping components; the seam is accepted and filed.</li><li>2,121 lines of code across 16 files — over the guidance, stated.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>Linear&#x27;s settings rebuild groups by *Features · Administration · Your teams* and shows members only what they own; Stripe organises the whole dashboard around jobs, not objects; LaunchDarkly separates project-wide filters from environment-specific ones and lets you compare a flag across environments side by side. The depth we are missing is elsewhere: Restaurant365 makes every unit resolve to one of three measure types and models a *receive unit* separately, Ottimate routes approvals by user, vendor, GL and dollar amount, and the whole field stores vendor cutoffs, delivery days and minimums as configuration. &quot;More&quot; here means a Vendor-terms tab, approval thresholds, a settings audit trail — and every control stating its blast radius.</p></div>
      <div class="block proof"><div class="label">Proof</div><ul><li>vitest 22/22 (was 14/15)</li><li>jest 23/23 organizations + settings (5 new)</li><li>tsc clean in owned modules · guard PASS (real run, dir in SCAN_ROOTS) · emoji grep empty</li><li>zero raw hex · zero fetch( · zero framer-motion</li><li>Sonnet re-audit: pass — five blockers closed, one citation narrowed; a real production defect (team roster ordered by a missing column) found and being fixed on its own PR</li></ul></div>
      <div class="decide" data-slug="settings">

<section class="entry" id="profile">
  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/profile</div>
    <h2>Profile — a seven-register account ledger</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">KEEP+ · third pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_profile · off</span><span class="chip pass">47 web · 60 billing + 79 mcp gateway tests</span><span class="chip pass">Builds A + D audited: pass, all findings closed</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="profile"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Profile — a seven-register account ledger — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Profile — a seven-register account ledger — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>Let&#x27;s make this a lot cooler. Must include MCPs — connected model-context servers as a first-class section; linked accounts — to be cooler than this, not just like that; payments — we should be able to add the payment here, Stripe or comparable.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Keep, with three additions · 2026-08-29</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>Second pass, to your ask (“almost identical to the ones $100B+ startups have — add MCP servers, payment types”): the ledger grew from four registers to seven — Who you are · Security · What is connected to you · Model context (MCP) · Payment types · The house · Ruled off — and the first screen tallies only the registers that actually answered. The one structural idea is unchanged and load-bearing: one ConnectionRow draws every row in all seven registers, so a live MCP server and a not-yet-built passkey differ only by their chip and by whether the control is live or disabled with its reason.</p><p>What became real: Model context is a true register (list · add · revoke) over a new gateway module and table; Payment types has a real table and routes, and “Add a card” opens the form but its submit is disabled with the provider&#x27;s stated reason (no Stripe key) and writes nothing; Security lists the password row, one evidence-built session row and four protections that do not exist yet, each with its measurement; the plan reads the real tier instead of an em dash; the restaurant-record read is now role-gated on the server, so the page&#x27;s permission line states a server rule.</p><p>Third pass (large builds A and D): Stripe is the live payment provider (ADR 0110) — nothing in the repo had ever spoken to Stripe, so the earlier “everything except the credential is built” was false; now a billing module holds SetupIntents, a customer per restaurant, a mirror of the provider&#x27;s instruments (never a card number), a signed webhook, detach-first removal and a default-method route, and the provider is itself a row in the same shape as every other attachment, naming each of its three secrets so “a secret is set” and “a seam works” read as different states. No charge can be built: the client throws before any payment, subscription, invoice or refund request, because pricing is still open. The MCP register became a list of readings (ADR 0107): pressing “Check the server” performs the real handshake with a timeout and caps, stores status, the server&#x27;s own name and version, and its tool names; the per-connection secret is encrypted at rest and never returned; tool invocation is deliberately absent until the commitment guardrail is extended to it.</p></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>MCP and Payments as full dead forms (server URL field, card field, plan picker) — the bigger gesture; rejected because a full dead form is exactly the shape the honesty rule exists to stop. Now moot: both registers have real storage behind them.</li><li>Connecting Stripe now with test keys so “Add a card” succeeds — not built: pricing is deferred (OD-23), and a provider connected before there is a price is a surface that can take money for nothing. Your call when pricing lands.</li><li>The MCP handshake (calling a connected server) — not built: no token column until the transport and credential fork is decided; the register records connections, it does not yet exercise them.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>The MCP read throws on a query error instead of returning an empty list — the opposite of the integrations read that forces the Workspace rail to infer failure from silence.</li><li>Four security protections (passkeys, 2FA, session revoke-all, API tokens) render as not built with the measurement that proved it; one session row is built from the evidence the token carries.</li><li>The location read now refuses non-managers on the server (404 before 403, so a restaurant outside the org does not leak); the copy states that rule.</li><li>The Stripe Elements mount and confirmSetup were not exercised in a live browser (a real test key must be baked in at dev-server start); everything up to that line is verified and the page&#x27;s copy says which secret unlocks it.</li><li>No tool invocation from the MCP register: no call route, a structural test that none exists, and the row prints the refusal in the gateway&#x27;s own words.</li><li>The MCP endpoint guard is now a byte-level parser that resolves names before the call and pins the vetted address into the socket — the mapped-IPv6 bypass the audit found is closed, with a test per literal form.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>Nobody in restaurant back-office competes on this page — MarketMan, MarginEdge and R365 treat the profile as a name-and-password form — so the references are outside the category. Stripe&#x27;s account model (team &amp; security, branding, SSO, and a checklist that names what is still missing before you can go live) is the payments shape to borrow; Claude&#x27;s Connectors panel is the MCP shape — a list of connected services, each reviewable, reconfigurable, revocable, never a JSON file. Linear shows how far preferences can go and also where to stop. The move that is ours alone: make this a permissions ledger — everything acting on your behalf, its scope, its last action — and, later, the user&#x27;s own record of what they sealed.</p></div>
      <div class="block proof"><div class="label">Proof</div><ul><li>tsc clean, web + gateway</li><li>five guards PASS incl. new-tables-locked-down</li><li>emoji grep empty</li><li>two new gateway modules + two migrations (094500, 094600)</li><li>vitest 47/47 · jest 60 (billing + payment-methods) + 79 (mcp-connections + mcp-runtime)</li><li>gateway boots with BillingModule registered · all guards PASS</li><li>curl: /billing/provider 200 / 401; setup-intent 503 without a key; webhook refusal 200 received:false naming the failing check</li><li>Builds A + D audited: pass — D&#x27;s mapped-IPv6 SSRF bypass closed (33 guard tests, address pinned into the socket); A&#x27;s webhook retry path pinned by five mutation-proven tests (65 billing tests)</li></ul></div>

  <header class="entry-head">
    <div class="route">/cellar · /wines · /beer · /whiskey · /cocktails</div>
    <h2>The Cellar — a cellar book, not a grid</h2>
    <div class="chips"><span class="chip ">IA decided · third pass</span><span class="chip flag">flag mudavym_design_cellar · off</span><span class="chip pass">59 web · 44+36 gateway tests</span><span class="chip pass">Build C audited: pass</span></div>
  </header>
  <div class="entry-body">
    <figure class="shot" data-slug="cellar"><img class="paper" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="The Cellar — a cellar book, not a grid — paper ground, 1440 wide"><img class="charcoal" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="The Cellar — a cellar book, not a grid — Warm Charcoal ground" hidden><figcaption><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="paper">Paper</button><button type="button" class="ground-toggle" data-ground="charcoal">Charcoal</button><span class="cap">captured 2026-09-02 · Meyhouse Palo Alto</span></figcaption></figure>
    <aside class="rail">
      <div class="block verdict"><div class="label">The verdict you gave</div><blockquote>I don&#x27;t like the new version. It&#x27;s so much crowded and I don&#x27;t like the way it looks… put more character into it. — and the IA: Cellar is the parent surface; /wines, /beer, /whiskey, /cocktails are its children.</blockquote><div class="verdict-kind">Reject the design, keep the breadth · 2026-08-29/30</div></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">What this build does with it</div><p>[&quot;Second pass, to your asks (every house is different; infer at onboarding then confirm; handle a category added later; show two more sketches). Which registers a house carries is now a per-tenant row in its own table — inferred · confirmed · manual, with the confirmation date empty exactly while it is still a guess — instead of a module constant. The page shows only the registers that are on, with one line saying how that was decided and where to change it: a non-alcoholic house sees Non-alcoholic and Soft drinks and no wine rack at all. The readout keeps four states apart that used to collapse into one: confirmed · inferred · unknown (all seven drawn, none claimed) · unread.\n\nThe library&#x27;s beverage kind finally reaches the browser, so beer, whisky, cocktails, spirits, non-alcoholic and soft drinks are counted from what the catalogue already knows (596 wines · 801 spirits · 272 whiskies · 87 beers · 33 cocktails · 20 non-alcoholic, live; 39 sake and 4 cider reported as unmapped) over new read-only beverage and cocktail routes. Two exported pieces: the onboarding confirm step and the Settings control (already mounted under Settings → Cellar). The prompt for a register switched on with no items is the backtested inline notice: register-aware, aggregated when several switch on at once, with the symmetric off-with-items band so nothing is lost.&quot;, &#x27;\n&#x27;, &#x27;\n&#x27;, &#x27;T&#x27;, &#x27;h&#x27;, &#x27;i&#x27;, &#x27;r&#x27;, &#x27;d&#x27;, &#x27;       <div class="block"><div class="label">Two roads not taken</div><ul><li>1 · The cellar floor — /cellar as a plan of the room, storage locations as zones, a register reached by walking the floor. The most characterful reading of “what is in the building”, and it fits the charcoal ground. Not built because storage_locations is exactly the table the seeded-defaults incident corrupted: 87 rows across 7 tenants, 84 carrying one of four invented zone names. A floor plan today would be a picture of fabricated data; it becomes the best parent the moment locations are trustworthy.</li><li>2 · One flat register with a kind facet — drop the four child routes, give the wine register a Beer/Whiskey/Cocktails filter. Not built because beverage_kind is computed in the database and dropped by the gateway before it reaches the browser, so the facet would have nothing to filter on, and a filter returning nothing reads as “no beer” rather than “no endpoint”. A live fork against the four-child IA if the gateway ever carries the field.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block"><div class="label">Honest about</div><ul><li>The registers write path is proven to fail correctly (a reason in words) but not yet to succeed locally: the shared database lacks the table until the migration merges — one live re-verification is filed for after.</li><li>A live bug caught while curling: an empty type list degraded to no filter and returned whiskies under soft drinks — fixed and tested.</li><li>The onboarding mount of the confirm step lives outside the page&#x27;s paths and is being wired separately; the three routeless registers (spirits, non-alcoholic, soft drinks) have no route yet, filed.</li><li>No move/hide action for items stranded in a register switched off — that needs a bulk write that does not exist; they stay visible under “not on the list”.</li><li>OD-113 (the ledger&#x27;s non-wine identity) stays open: a declared beer register can be counted from the catalogue but not stocked until it is decided — the page says so.</li></ul></div>
      <div class="block lens"><div class="label">Competitor lens</div><p>BinWise runs the serious restaurant cellar — POS-depleted bottles, deadstock and PAR alerts, valuation by cost or retail, a guest-facing list published from inventory. Backbar gives away a 300,000-item database plus staff flashcards; Provi and SevenFifty put 750,000 products behind filters for region, vintage and price; CellarTracker adds 7.5 million tasting notes and fifteen years of valuation, while stating plainly that its values are estimates. Competing on catalogue size is a losing game — theirs is every wine, ours is *this house&#x27;s* five hundred. The character the page is missing is not more chrome: it is the house&#x27;s own record on each row — first bought, what we&#x27;ve paid, what we&#x27;ve poured, who quoted it — with an em dash where we don&#x27;t know.</p></div>

  <footer class="foot">
    <h3>What a call does</h3>
    <p>Keep sends the page to a Sonnet audit already passed and a two-Opus review, then a PR to main with its flag still OFF; you flip it per restaurant in Settings when you want it live.</p><p>Rework means I redraw from your note: I will build the direction you name, or the one of the two roads not taken you point at, and bring it back here.</p><p>Merge means today&#x27;s page still holds something the rebuild lost; say what, and the rebuild absorbs it.</p><p>Hold parks the page as it is, flag OFF, nothing merged.</p><p>The four large builds ship dark twice over: behind each page&#x27;s design flag, and — for reminders and Stripe — behind an environment switch (CALENDAR_REMINDERS_ENABLED; the three Stripe secrets), because each writes to the world outside the house. Nothing merges to main until you say so.</p>
  </footer>

<script>
(() => {
  const rm = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
  document.querySelectorAll('.shot').forEach((fig) => {
    const paper = fig.querySelector('img.paper'), charcoal = fig.querySelector('img.charcoal');
    const btns = fig.querySelectorAll('.ground-toggle');
    const set = (g) => { if (!charcoal) g = 'paper'; paper.hidden = g === 'charcoal'; charcoal && (charcoal.hidden = g !== 'charcoal'); btns.forEach(b => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.ground === g))); };
    btns.forEach(b => { b.addEventListener('click', () => set(b.dataset.ground)); if (!charcoal && b.dataset.ground === 'charcoal') { b.disabled = true; b.title = 'charcoal capture not taken'; } });
    set('paper');
  });
  const local = {};
  document.querySelectorAll('.decide').forEach((box) => {
    const slug = box.dataset.slug, choices = box.querySelectorAll('.choices button'), note = box.querySelector('textarea'), save = box.querySelector('.save'), status = box.querySelector('.status');
    local[slug] = { verdict: null };
    choices.forEach(b => b.addEventListener('click', () => { local[slug].verdict = b.dataset.verdict; choices.forEach(x => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(x === b))); }));
    save.disabled = true; status.textContent = 'connecting…';
    box._apply = (d) => { if (!d) return; local[slug].verdict = d.verdict || null; choices.forEach(x => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(x.dataset.verdict === d.verdict))); if (typeof d.note === 'string' && document.activeElement !== note) note.value = d.note; status.textContent = d.at ? 'recorded ' + new Date(d.at).toLocaleString() : ''; };
    box._wire = (db) => {
      const ref = db.doc('verdicts/' + slug);
      ref.onSnapshot((snap) => box._apply(snap.exists ? snap.data() : null), () => { status.textContent = 'could not read the record'; });
      save.disabled = false; status.textContent = '';
      save.addEventListener('click', async () => {
        if (!local[slug].verdict) { status.textContent = 'pick a call first'; return; }
        save.disabled = true; status.textContent = 'recording…';
        try { await ref.set({ verdict: local[slug].verdict, note: note.value, at: new Date().toISOString(), page: slug }); status.textContent = 'recorded'; }
        catch (e) { status.textContent = 'not recorded — ' + (e && e.code ? e.code : 'error'); }
        finally { save.disabled = false; }
      });
    };
  });
  (async () => {
    const db = window.claude && typeof window.claude.use === 'function' ? await window.claude.use('db') : null;
    document.querySelectorAll('.decide').forEach((box) => {
      if (db) box._wire(db); else { box.querySelector('.status').textContent = 'recording unavailable in this view — tell me your call in chat'; }
    });
  })();
})();
</script>
